mechanism_narrative: A sustained 6-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) signals weakening consumer demand, which depresses corporate earnings expectations and drives S&P 500 forward returns downward over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances, or Rank IC exceeds 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average signals expansion in manufacturing output, which boosts corporate earnings and drives S&P 500 forward returns upward over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances, or Rank IC remains below 0.04 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 1-month rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5.0% signals a tightening monetary cycle that increases discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances, or Rank IC exceeds 0.06 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% signals labor market weakness, which depresses corporate earnings and drives S&P 500 forward returns downward over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances, or Rank IC remains below 0.04 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average signals expansion in residential construction activity, which boosts corporate earnings and drives S&P 500 forward returns upward over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances, or Rank IC remains below 0.04 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 1-month rise in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% signals inflationary pressures that prompt the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates, increasing discount rates applied to equity cash flows and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances, or Rank IC exceeds 0.06 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) below its 12-month moving average signals weakening consumer demand, which depresses corporate earnings and drives S&P 500 forward returns downward over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances, or Rank IC exceeds 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% signals labor market weakness, which depresses corporate earnings and drives S&P 500 forward returns downward over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances, or Rank IC remains below 0.04 over any 2-year rolling window.
